questions.q: In the query/key/value framing of attention, what does the key represent?
options: What a position is looking for
What a position has to offer when compared against a query
The final output of the attention layer
The loss function used during training
questions.explain: The key is compared against queries to produce relevance scores — it represents what a position offers, which may or may not match what a given query is looking for.

questions.q: In scaled dot-product attention, what operation turns raw relevance scores into attention weights?
options: A ReLU activation
Softmax along the last dimension
Batch normalization
Dividing by the batch size
questions.explain: Softmax converts the raw Q·Kᵗ scores into a probability distribution per query row, so the weights on each row sum to 1.

questions.q: Why are attention scores divided by sqrt(d_k) before the softmax?
options: To make the computation run faster on GPU
Because PyTorch requires it as a function argument
To keep dot-product magnitudes stable as d_k grows, preventing softmax from saturating into a near one-hot distribution
To convert the scores into probabilities directly, replacing softmax
questions.explain: Dot products of higher-dimensional vectors tend to have larger magnitude; scaling by sqrt(d_k) keeps scores in a range where softmax gradients don't vanish.

questions.q: In the manual attention function, what shape does the output of attention(q, k, v) have, given q, k, v are all (batch, seq_len, d_k)?
options: (batch, seq_len, d_k) — same as v
(batch, seq_len, seq_len)
(seq_len, seq_len)
(batch, d_k)
questions.explain: The intermediate scores matrix is (batch, seq_len, seq_len), but the final matmul with v brings it back to (batch, seq_len, d_k) — the same shape as v.

questions.q: What does torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention provide compared to the hand-written attention function?
options: Completely different math, better suited for images
The same mathematical operation, fused and optimized, with built-in attn_mask and is_causal support
A way to skip the softmax step entirely
A replacement for nn.Linear layers
questions.explain: It computes the same scaled dot-product attention, just as a fused, memory-efficient kernel, with convenient masking and causal-attention options built in.
